newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits little changed in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits little changed in late trade.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were little changed in moderate trade on Thursday, dealers said.

They said most traders were sitting on the sidelines and waiting for tonight's release of the U.S. weekly jobless claims data, second quarter gross domestic product (GDP) and July Chicago purchasing managers index (PMI) data.
Weekly jobless claims for the week ended July 26 are forecast to be around 306,000 compared with 299,000 reported in the previous week.
The second quarter GDP is expected to decline to a 1.9 percent rise against the first quarter's 5.9 percent increase.
The Chicago PMI for July is expected to ease to 59.8 from 61.5 in June.

"The market was quiet and featureless in the morning on some position adjustments. Some traders are waiting for fresh clues to market direction from tonight's release of the weekly jobless claims, second quarter GDP and (July) Chicago PMI figures," a local dealer said.
"The numbers have been built into the market and most people have squared their positions for the day, so I don't think there will be much impact," he said.

In day-to-day rates, Thursday/Friday was unchanged from Wednesday's 5-13/16 5-11/16 percent, weekend eased 3/16 percentage point to 5-5/8 5-1/2 percent and week-fixed was unchanged at 5-5/8 5-1/2 percent.

Among longer dates, two-months was unchanged at 5-11/16 5-9/16 percent, six-months unchanged at 5-13/16 5-11/16, nine-months unchanged at 5-7/8 5-3/4 and twelve-months unchanged at 5-15/16 5-13/16 percent.
